summary: Jake H. Davis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a PhD from CUNY, also studying under several Sayadaws. He has held appointments at Brown University, NYU, and CUNY.
Jakob Bucher worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a missionary with the Basel Mission and as superintendent of the Anglo-Vernacular High School in 1890.
Jakob H. Thiessen is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Kiel University between 1875 and 1880 under the supervision of Richard Pischel.

Jakob Halfmann specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held the Chair of Comparative Philology at the University of Würzburg (2023–2025) and became a group leader at the Free University of Berlin in 2026.

Jakob Hausheer studied at the University of Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler and Adolf Kaegi, and earned his Ph.D. from Halle-Wittenberg in 1889. In 1905, he became ordinary Professor for Old Testament Studies and Oriental Languages at Zurich.

Jakob Steiner studied at Heidelberg University (1818–1821) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1822–1824). He held posts at Beuth Hochschule für Technik Berlin (1825–1834) and Frederick William University Berlin (1834–1863).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Oxford and the University of Tübingen, completing a Ph.D. and habilitation under Richard von Garbe. He held chairs at the University of Marburg (1925–1927) and Tübingen (1927–1945).
Jakub Čejka is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied at Charles University, completing an MA (1990–1998) and a BA in 2018.

James A. Benn specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and has served as Associate Professor and Professor of Religious Studies at McMaster University.
James A. Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He served as Professor of Religion and Chair of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 1998, 2007).
James Adam was a scholar of philosophy who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1876–1880) and Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge (~1880–1884).

James Alan Matisoff is a linguist specializing in sinology and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard, International Christian University, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1967). After teaching at Columbia (1966–1969), he became Professor Emeritus at UC Berkeley (1970–2002).

James Atkinson studied at the University of Edinburgh and worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He held posts as Assistant Surgeon in the Indian Medical Service, Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College, and Deputy Assay Master in Kolkata.

James B. Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1996 under John D. Dunne, studying also with numerous traditional and academic teachers.

James Bird studied at the University of Aberdeen and Guy's and St Thomas'. A scholar of Indology and archaeology, he served as assistant surgeon in the Bombay Presidency and secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (1844–1847).

James Bissett Pratt worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Williams College and Harvard (Ph.D. under William James), he served as Professor of Intellectual and Moral Philosophy at Williams College from 1917 to 1943.

James Blumenthal was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He served as an associate professor at Oregon State University and professor at Maitripa College.
James Bradstreet Greenough was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard University (A.B. 1852–1856) and later served there as Tutor of Latin from 1865 to 1873.

James Burgess studied at Glasgow and Edinburgh, working in Indology and archaeology. He was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1886–1889), taught mathematics at Doveton College, and edited the Indian Antiquary and Epigraphia Indica.

James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa (attested 1996).
